sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Slip-Form Reinforced Concrete Silo Slipforming and Aeration Towers

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction, including mainland and overseas departments subject to the same corporate law framework)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Unitary National; Code Civil and Code de Commerce as primary codified sources; jurisprudence administrative and commercial case-law as secondary interpretive guidance)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France maintains more than 100 active bilateral investment treaties (BITs) and over 70 double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAAs). The precise treaty applicable to the shareholder/UBO is determined after final UBO residence identification.
Example active treaties: France–China BIT, France–Algeria BIT, France–Morocco BIT, France–UAE BIT, France–United States DTAA (1994, as amended by 2006 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq., as amended by Ordinance No. 2020-115 and Decree No. 2021-1091 of 17 August 2021, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Code de commerce (C. com.), Articles L.123-31-1 and R.123-140-3 et seq.; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing obligation integrated in the RCS formation process.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statuts de la Société / SARL Articles of Association (if executed or signed abroad by a shareholder, each signature must be authenticated)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin for notarized articles; otherwise legal counsel with original signatures for private articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (France and most relevant source countries are Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); for non-Hague states, consular legalization by the French Consulate in the source country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing (or equivalent) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry / competent corporate authority in the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted by each shareholder for the person signing on formation documents and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for all UBOs and statutory management members (Gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the relevant country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / banker's identification confirmation for share capital funding and payment rails (Milestone Wire or Letter of Credit)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's bank (must issue within 30 days of registration; language must be French or accompanied by certified translation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required if issued on bank letterhead in French or English; otherwise apostille/consular legalization for non-Hague ad hoc certifications

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence arises under CMF Article L.561-10 for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) defined in Article L.561-2. The French corporate service provider must screen all identified shareholders, UBOs, managers (Gérants) and authorized representatives against: (1) French asset-freeze and financial management measures operated by DGDDI/DG Trésor; (2) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Taric); (3) United Nations Security Council sanctions listings; (4) Interpol notices where relevant; and (5) OFAC SDN list when USD clearing is anticipated. Screening must produce a time-stamped audit trail, negative-match confirmation, and a written AML/CFT risk assessment before filing of the RCS application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); public company registry data accessible via infogreffe.fr / Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name (dénomination sociale) and all constitutive documents must be in French pursuant to Article 2 of the French Constitution and Article L.123-1 et seq. C. com. Non-Latin script UBO names and foreign corporate names must be transliterated into Latin script in all French filings; the registered name must have a clear French phonetic and spelling form and cannot be rendered solely in Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic or other non-Latin ideogrammatic script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI/RNCS registrar (greffier du tribunal de commerce) refuses the proposed name for similarity, prohibited token, or public-order grounds, the applicant may: (1) within one month, file a formal administrative petition (recours gracieux) before the President of the competent Commercial Court under Article R.123-3 C. com., attaching the refusal notice, a conflict search report, and the proposed revised name; (2) request an order by the President compelling registration (procédure gracieuse); (3) otherwise institute an action before the Tribunal de commerce for reversal and damages. Simultaneously, the applicant may modify the name and immediately resubmit through the Guichet Unique; the 30-day reservation window is not renewable unless a new filing action is commenced and no adverse third-party filing has occurred.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Approved domiciliation services are permissible under Article L.123-11-2 C. com. for the first year only unless the agreement permits continued domiciliation with a qualified business hub. For an ISIC 4100 grain-silo EPC construction entity, French tax and social authorities require demonstrable commercial substance (an operational site office, storage yard, or construction site address). A purely virtual Paris address is accepted for registration but is treated as a red flag and may be reclassified for tax purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a newly registered SARL in a low AML-risk agricultural construction sector, estimated at <5% per year of unannounced on-site inspection by inspection du travail, URSSAF authorities, or tax control where no adverse indicators are present; risk rises to approximately 12-15% if the registered office is virtual-only and no construction site or physical facility can be evidenced.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official RCS registration fee through Guichet Unique / INPI (dénomination sociale, Kbis initial issuing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce compétent / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated tariff fixed by decree for greffier services (tarif des greffiers de tribunaux de commerce)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal formation announcement (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff (minimum rate sometimes capped by order; typical range EUR 140–220)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/Consular legalization package for five foreign corporate and UBO documents (power of attorney, certificates, identity, bank reference)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in the document's country of origin, Hague Apostille authority, and/or French Consulate if non-Hague member

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L223-1 to L223-43 and R223-1 to R223-36 governing Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Articles L561-46 et seq. governing beneficial-owner disclosure; French Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq. governing companies generally.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for registration of a société à responsabilité limitée through the INPI Guichet unique, together with the déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs and supporting constitutional documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies. The amount must be stated in the articles. For cash contributions, at least 20% must be paid upon incorporation and the balance within five years of registration. Contributions are deposited before filing with an authorised bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, which issues a deposit certificate. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed and may require an independent contribution auditor unless the statutory waiver conditions are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and record the subscription by each shareholder for the quotas allocated under the articles, with the cash contributions deposited as evidenced by the deposit certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address] and remain effective until lawfully changed. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Gérant for an unlimited term, with authority to represent the Company and complete all incorporation, banking, tax, employment, licensing, and commercial formalities. RESOLVED, that [name] be authorised to file, correct, and sign all documents required by the INPI Guichet unique, the RCS, and other competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate identity, activities, and ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique and competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the French legal name, verify availability, define the registered office, confirm the principal activity and appropriate NAF code, identify shareholders and the manager, and map direct and indirect beneficial ownership. Obtain certified translations where documents are not in French and legalise or apostille foreign public documents when required.
required_dossiers: Manager identity documents and signed declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Corporate shareholder certificates and powers of attorney
French activity description and NAF classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the activity, identity, address, ownership, or translation defects identified by the registry; upload a complete replacement package through the INPI portal within the prescribed cure period and retain the electronic filing receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute articles and arrange capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised deposit bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles of association and shareholder subscription schedule. Open a temporary capital-deposit account, transfer the subscribed cash capital, obtain the certificate of deposit, and retain evidence of any contribution in kind. Signatures may be electronic where legally acceptable; foreign execution documents should be notarised and apostilled or legalised when required.
required_dossiers: Shareholder resolutions or powers of attorney
Independent contribution auditor report or waiver statement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries by supplying ownership, source-of-funds, identification, and corporate-authority evidence; correct execution defects and obtain a new deposit certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A journal habilité à publier des annonces légales in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory formation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, manager identity, and registration details. Pay the regulated publication charge and obtain the attestation de parution. The notice must be published before the RCS registration application.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or certified corporate particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request immediate correction or republication of any incomplete or inaccurate mandatory particulars and attach the corrected publication certificate to the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for RCS registration and beneficial-owner disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for transmission to the competent RCS commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic incorporation application, upload the signed articles, capital certificate, publication certificate, registered-office evidence, manager declaration, identification documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the applicable registry and beneficial-owner charges. Monitor the portal for requests for supplemental information.
required_dossiers: Manager declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Foreign-company documents and certified French translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically to the registry query, replace defective documents, pay any additional fee, and request reinstatement or clarification from the greffe if the application is rejected. A formal challenge or appeal may be filed under applicable procedural rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, French tax administration (Direction générale des finances publiques), and the deposit bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract, provide it to the bank to release the capital, activate the permanent account, register for applicable VAT and corporate-tax obligations, establish accounting records, and implement annual accounts and management-report procedures. Register employees with the applicable social bodies before hiring.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or bank onboarding discrepancies using the Kbis and constitutional file; submit amended tax registrations or declarations through the relevant administration portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain construction, industrial, environmental, and operating clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mairie, Préfet of the department, DREAL or DRIEAT, SDIS, and applicable labour and inspection authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before construction or operation, classify the proposed grain silo and related installations under the ICPE nomenclature, determine whether declaration, registration, or authorisation applies, obtain the required building permit, complete environmental review, and secure fire, explosion-risk, structural, and workplace compliance. Do not commence regulated operation before the relevant permit or prefectural decision is effective.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact or examination dossier, if required
Dust, noise, wastewater, and waste-management assessments
Occupational risk assessment and operating procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address requests for additional information, amend the design, undertake public consultation or environmental review where required, and challenge an adverse prefectural or municipal decision through the applicable administrative appeal route.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Préfet of the department, generally assisted by the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), or Direction régionale et interdépartementale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et des transports (DRIEAT) in the Île-de-France region. The competent Mairie issues the construction permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or authorisation for grain and cereal storage installations under the applicable ICPE nomenclature, particularly rubrique 2160. The applicable level depends on storage capacity, materials, configuration, and associated processing equipment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, through the competent regional environmental authority (Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale or Conseil général de l'environnement et du développement durable, as applicable), with DREAL or DRIEAT technical review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific. A grain silo is not automatically subject to a full EIA solely because it is a SARL activity. The project may require a systematic environmental assessment, a case-by-case examination, or no EIA depending on the Environmental Code thresholds, ICPE regime, capacity, location, protected areas, and associated works.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE prefectural order and sectoral requirements, including dust and particulate-emission controls, explosion-risk and ATEX measures, sealed transfer systems, filtration, noise limits, wastewater discharge authorisation, spill prevention, and traceable hazardous and non-hazardous waste handling. Numerical limits are fixed by the applicable ICPE category and prefectural order rather than by the corporate form.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the applicable construction permit and completion conformity evidence from the Mairie; provide fire-safety design and emergency-access information to the Service départemental d'incendie et de secours (SDIS); complete structural and equipment inspections by competent inspection bodies; implement ATEX zoning, dust-explosion protection, machinery conformity, electrical safety, evacuation, and emergency procedures; and comply with the French Labour Code, occupational-risk assessment, workplace health and safety, and mandatory inspection requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate-General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), administered through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official tax portal impots.gouv.fr. Corporate formation and business-registration filings are submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is formed through the INPI Guichet unique, which transmits the formation filing to the competent registries and public authorities. Following registration, the entity receives a SIREN number for the legal entity, a SIRET number for each establishment, and an intracommunity VAT number beginning with FR. The DGFiP assigns or confirms the corporate tax account and VAT obligations through the competent SIE. The company must provide its articles of association, registration extract, registered-office evidence, directors' and shareholders' information, business activity description, bank details where requested, and beneficial-owner information. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in France must obtain a French SIREN/SIRET and VAT registration through the INPI process or the competent foreign-entity tax service, generally the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères, depending on the activity and filing circumstances. An EU-established business may use the OSS regime for eligible cross-border B2C supplies but must obtain French VAT registration where French domestic VAT obligations, local establishments, imports, or non-OSS transactions require it. VAT identification can be verified through the EU VIES system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). An SARL satisfying statutory conditions may elect for partnership-style income taxation (impôt sur le revenu, IR), including an election available to certain newly formed companies for a limited period and a family-SARL election where all shareholders are qualifying family members and the statutory conditions are met. The election is made with the competent tax authority and is subject to eligibility, timing, and revocation rules. France has no general US-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD II can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize arrangements involving hybrid entities or instruments and related-party or structured transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), with customs import VAT and separate domestic accounting and reporting obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no universal VAT registration threshold for all taxable businesses. Taxable supplies in France generally create VAT obligations unless an exemption applies. The domestic French franchise en base de TVA may apply to eligible small businesses below the applicable statutory turnover thresholds, generally EUR 25,000 of prior-year turnover and EUR 27,500 of current-year turnover for the general activities threshold under the current framework, subject to activity-specific thresholds, legislative changes, and transitional rules. A business exceeding the applicable threshold, opting for ordinary VAT treatment, importing goods, making transactions requiring a VAT number, or otherwise falling outside the franchise must register and comply with VAT obligations. Construction activities may also trigger sector-specific invoicing, reverse-charge, and subcontracting rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and electronic transaction-data reporting through approved private platforms or the public platform designated under the reform. All French businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuing obligations apply from 1 September 2026 to large companies and in-scope intermediate-sized enterprises and from 1 September 2027 to small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises, subject to the legally applicable timetable. France generally operates a post-transaction reporting model rather than universal real-time invoice clearance. Cross-border B2B transactions and B2C transactions may require electronic reporting of transaction data and, where relevant, payment data. Invoices must satisfy French VAT content, authenticity, integrity, and retention requirements. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Import and export customs declarations are submitted electronically through the French customs systems, principally DELTA IE and related customs services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT under Article 262 I of the French Tax Code where the supplier, an authorized intermediary, or the customer completes the export formalities and the goods physically leave the EU customs territory. The supplier must retain reliable evidence linking the commercial invoice, goods, export declaration, and exit confirmation. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are transported from France to that Member State, and the supplier holds the required VAT numbers and transport evidence. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore. B2B services are generally located at the customer's establishment under the EU place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT, while specific services, including services connected with French immovable property, remain taxable in France. Construction and installation services connected with immovable property must be analyzed according to the place-of-supply rules and may not qualify as exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, contractual terms, and VAT treatment
Electronic export declaration accepted by French customs, including the Movement Reference Number or equivalent customs reference
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent evidence that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
Transport document, such as a bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or carrier delivery record
Packing list and, where applicable, proof of loading and delivery
Purchase order, contract, and payment evidence linking the shipment to the transaction
For intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and transport evidence
For VAT refunds, VAT invoices, import VAT documents, accounting records, and proof that the claimant incurred the VAT in the course of taxable business activities
An inward-remittance certificate is not a general French statutory requirement for claiming export VAT exemption; banking evidence may nevertheless support the commercial substance and audit trail.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. Export VAT exemption or deduction may be denied or clawed back if the supplier cannot prove physical export, valid customer status, transport, customs exit, or the taxable-business connection. The DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties. The standard penalty for an intentional breach may be 40 percent of the reassessed tax, while fraudulent conduct may attract an 80 percent penalty, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Failure to produce records can result in rejection of the exemption, estimated assessment, or reversal of input VAT recovery. False customs declarations may also trigger customs recovery, customs penalties, seizure measures, and potentially criminal liability. Repeated or deliberate VAT fraud may result in criminal prosecution and additional financial penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as national central bank; foreign exchange and balance-of-payments regulatory competence is shared with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance, and Recovery.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the euro on both current and capital account by virtue of French law and Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; no foreign exchange control authorization is required for inbound capital injection, trade settlement, profit distribution, or cross-border borrowing. Profit remittance by a French SARL is structurally unencumbered at the FX level; the only practical constraints are corporate law (répartition of distributable profits) and the applicable dividend withholding tax (25% statutory, up to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or treaty exemption).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts under the French Code monétaire et financier; since the 1990 liberalization, exporters may freely retain proceeds in foreign currency or convert to euros. The sole compliance duty is statistical: the importing/exporting bank must include transactions in the balance-of-payments report to Banque de France (using BPM6-compliant purpose codes) for threshold-exceeding operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Fonds de dépôt) and Operational Account
Operational Account (Euro/USD Multi-Currency) and Milestone Deposit Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance/Treasury Line
Operational Account and Domestic/Countertrade Settlement Account
Operational Account and Subsidized Construction Escrow Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low for complete treasury orchestration: ACPR-licensed and EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 can provide efficient SEPA/instant cross-border payment rail, multi-currency IBANs, and expense management, and are viable as a secondary operational payment layer. However, EMIs in France are legally barred from deposit-taking, credit intermediation, and issuing documentary credits; they cannot independently issue commercial letters of credit, guarantees, or URDG instruments, and settlement through an EMI still requires a partner credit institution for SWIFT MT103 correspondent clearing and for capital-escrow certification. For the grain-silo EPC model (milestone wires and LCs), a fully licensed credit institution remains mandatory as primary treasury counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default norm for non-resident directors/shareholders: French banks almost uniformly require the gérant and each 25%-threshold beneficial owner to attend an in-person interview at a branch or a French notary/consular proxy for original ID verification, signature specimen, and UBO confirmation. Remote video onboarding (FALO/digital KYC) is tolerated only for simplified low-risk structures with tokenized ID validation and is practically unavailable to a construction company with a non-resident shareholder base and large milestone inflows; certified corporate documents must bear the apostille or consular legalization, plus registered French translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex cross-border holding chain with non-resident UBOs (opacity red flag under the French Code monétaire et financier Art. L.561-2).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized shareholder register, full ultimate-beneficial-ownership declaration filed to the Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, certified IDs with apostille/consular legalization, translated corporate constitutive documents, residency certificates for all UBOs, and a written treasury narrative naming the commercial rationale for each offshore layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Activity/ISIC mismatch: agricultural construction classified in a lower-risk band yet invoicing volumes incompatible with stated share capital and payslip count.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed EPC contract with work breakdown schedule, three-year business plan and cash-flow forecast, interim creditor/VAT filings, subcontractor licensing evidence, ISIC 4100 scope narrative, and evidence of fixed assets (slip-form rigs, tower cranes) consistent with the balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity outbound wires to jurisdictions with grain-export concentration and shipping-intermediary structures (e.g., opaque FZE counterparties or non-EU commodity corridors).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dual contract support (construction contract + downstream commodity sale/purchase), customs declarations (DAU/ENS), bill-of-lading archives, silo-site photographic geotagging, surveyor certificates, and counterparty KYB file with bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent third-party funds movements (client pays via a parent treasury center or commodity trader clearinghouse rather than from the documented client entity).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Irrevocable payment delegation letters from the actual funder to the contractual client, escrow agent statements, SWIFT MT103 chain, board minutes ratifying each payment instruction, and an amended contract recognizing the payment rail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections into the SARL must be executed by SWIFT MT103 wire to a French-domiciled blocked or operational account with clear remittance purpose 'RE: Capital Increase — SARL [Name]' and the French BOP/transmission purpose code corresponding to direct investment capital (P801/P802 under BPM6 classification). The funds are frozen in a depository (bank or notary) until the RCS registration or publication of the modification is completed; the bank issues a deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) required for the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce filing. For incoming EUR from EU parents, routing over TARGET2/SEPA (SCT) is frictionless; for USD and non-EUR funds, the bank converts or credits a foreign-currency working account as designated, with no prior FX authorization. Verification pack: shareholder resolution, appraisal report for in-kind contributions if any, signed capital increase deed (sous seing privé), and K-bis update after registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the silo elevator project are routed primarily over (i) SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for subcontractor payments, aeration-tower equipment suppliers, and freight/shipping charges; (ii) irrevocable commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) governed by ICC rules, with deferred or at-sight payment structured upon certificate of provisional acceptance, enabling counterparties to finance the lead time; and (iii) demand guarantees/standby LCs (URDG 758) for performance and advance-payment security. Euro-denominated disbursements settle instantly via SEPA Credit Transfer/SEPA Instant on the TARGET2 platform of Banque de France; US-dollar disbursements are cleared on the correspondent banking network of the Paris-based clearing bank (BIC correspondent/CHIPS). Each disbursement must embed the underlying invoice reference and export/import customs codes where cross-border surveillance applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards between EUR and USD/GBP/CHF for firm milestone receipts
FX swaps (swap de change) for temporary conversion of USD tender proceeds into EUR without altering the trading book
Cross-currency swaps covering long-tenor project financing matched to the EPC milestone schedule
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or low-liquidity currencies tied to grain-export corridors (e.g., certain Kazakh Tenge and other convertibility-limited pairs)
Optional OTC EUR/USD and EUR/GBP currency options for asymmetrical protection of bidding/tender pipelines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' general meeting approving the annual accounts (AGO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulatory filing; signed minutes and attendance sheet must be retained in the statutory corporate minute book at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; for a SARL with a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting allows any shareholder to petition the Commercial Court to summon the meeting at company expense; persistent default may support removal of the gérant and, in serious cases, judicial dissolution.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profits, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, paid-up capital requirements, and qualifying ownership. France also provides targeted tax credits and accelerated or exceptional depreciation regimes for qualifying investments; no general tax holiday applies to ordinary silo or elevator construction activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, accompanied by the corporate income tax package forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2058-E-SD, 2058-F-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and applicable supporting forms; electronic filing through the French tax authority professional portal, impots.gouv.fr espace professionnel, generally using EDI-TDFC or EFI where available.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; quarterly corporate income tax instalments for companies subject to instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and tax package are generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For financial years ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second business day after 1 May of the following year. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, tax office, financial year dates, legal form, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's own SIREN and registered office. Identify non-resident shareholders separately in corporate records and related-party disclosures; do not replace the SARL's identity with that of its foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable profit or loss and tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, applicable corporate income tax, reduced-rate profit where eligible, tax credits, instalments, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the SARL's worldwide taxable result under French corporate tax rules, subject to treaty allocation and foreign tax relief. Foreign parent profits are not included unless attributable to the French entity or a French permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling accounting profit to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify expenses involving foreign related parties, withholding taxes, permanent-establishment allocations, and expenses lacking French business purpose or supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward or back and losses used against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally attributable to the French SARL. Loss transfers within a French tax group require the relevant tax-consolidation regime and cannot be created solely through foreign-parent accounting entries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of provisions, capital gains, capital losses, and special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the tax basis, valuation, and business rationale for construction-contract provisions, warranty provisions, claims, impairment, and asset disposals.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of taxable income, applicable rates, credits, and corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate unless a specific statutory reduced rate or credit is demonstrably available. Treaty relief generally does not reduce French corporate tax on the SARL's own taxable profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on related entities, ownership, intra-group transactions, and tax group matters where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parent, sister companies, financing entities, procurement entities, management-service providers, and IP owners where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participations held, entities connected by ownership, and relevant ownership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign participations and the identity and jurisdiction of significant shareholders in accordance with the form instructions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2067-SD, non-deductible or exceptional management expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain management fees, commissions, extraordinary payments, and expenses requiring specific disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose material payments to foreign related parties and retain contracts, invoices, benefit evidence, allocation keys, and proof of services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, including research and development, apprenticeship, investment, or other qualifying credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by French eligibility conditions, contemporaneous records, and expenditure-level evidence; foreign parent expenditure is not automatically eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer-pricing return and, where applicable, country-by-country reporting notification or report.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use French reporting forms and thresholds. Maintain consistency between the tax return, statutory accounts, Local File, Master File, customs declarations, and intercompany agreements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% where the taxpayer fails to regularize after formal notice and potentially to 80% in cases involving fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive conduct. Late payment interest is generally 0.20% per month. Understatements may generate tax reassessment, interest, and penalties ranging from 10% to 80% depending on the taxpayer's conduct. False or incomplete reporting may create separate criminal tax-fraud exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% generally applies to dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder, subject to applicable treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions, and anti-abuse rules. French resident individual recipients are generally subject to a 12.8% income-tax withholding, with social contributions handled under separate rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test requirements, and the applicable treaty rate. The payer should retain the certificate, beneficial-owner declaration, ownership chain, payment records, and evidence of substance. Where French administrative procedure requires prior authorization or reduced-rate documentation, submit the prescribed form to the competent French tax office before applying the reduced rate. Otherwise, withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund using the applicable French refund procedure. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption requires qualifying EU residence, minimum participation and holding-period conditions, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction and possible exemption under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where all conditions are satisfied. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but a 75% rate may apply to payments to non-cooperative or non-transparent jurisdictions, subject to statutory exceptions. Treaty rates vary, commonly providing reduced or zero rates for qualifying interest and reduced rates for royalties. Beneficial ownership, anti-conduit, transfer-pricing, and principal-purpose requirements must be tested before applying treaty or EU relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million. French Local File and Master File obligations generally apply where the French entity or the relevant French tax group exceeds the statutory turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where the related foreign enterprise meets the corresponding conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone regime named Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance is nevertheless relevant under French transfer-pricing rules, the beneficial-ownership requirement, the general anti-abuse doctrine, the principal-purpose test in treaties, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, and EU anti-tax-avoidance measures. A French SARL should maintain genuine French decision-making, qualified personnel, premises or operational capacity appropriate to its construction activity, commercial risk control, contract management, technical supervision, and contemporaneous evidence of services received or supplied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing turnover, fabricating costs, omitting taxable income, manipulating construction margins, using false invoices, or knowingly filing materially inaccurate corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 40% or 80% tax penalties depending on conduct, late-payment interest, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment for up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000; aggravated cases may reach seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability, personal fines, management bans, civil liability for deliberate or serious tax misconduct, and liability under French tax recovery provisions. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from judicial measures or an outstanding criminal proceeding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management, engineering, procurement, financing, royalty, or guarantee fees; shifting construction profits offshore without functions and risk; or failing to provide required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's-length profit, late-payment interest, and documentation penalties that may be calculated by reference to the transaction amount or the reassessed adjustment, subject to statutory minimums and limits. Severe cases may also generate a 40% or 80% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for deliberate mismanagement, criminal exposure where documents are falsified or fraud is established, and personal liability for tax recovery where statutory conditions for management fault are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using offshore entities with no personnel or operational capacity to invoice nonexistent services, route profits, conceal beneficial owners, or create artificial debt and royalty deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, withholding-tax reassessment, anti-abuse adjustment, penalties of up to 80% in aggravated cases, potential fraud, forgery, fraudulent insolvency, or money-laundering prosecution, and possible corporate dissolution or management prohibition.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be personally prosecuted for participation, complicity, concealment, or money laundering; sanctions can include imprisonment, fines, asset confiscation, management bans, and civil restitution. A shell company is not unlawful solely because it is foreign or low-substance; the offense arises from its use for unlawful or abusive conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared Dividend, Interest, or Royalty Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying profits to foreign shareholders or related parties without applying French withholding, applying treaty relief without residence or beneficial-ownership evidence, or disguising dividends as deductible service fees or interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, penalties, potential denial of deductions, and joint or payer liability where French withholding obligations were not correctly performed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for deliberate withholding failures, fraudulent documentation, or participation in concealment. Civil and criminal consequences depend on intent and the amount involved.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying an incorrect VAT rate, omitting milestone invoices, misusing reverse-charge rules, issuing accommodation invoices, or failing to reconcile progress certificates, subcontractor invoices, and customer receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80%, invoice penalties, suspension of VAT numbers in serious cases, and criminal prosecution for organized or fraudulent schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally liable for intentional VAT fraud, false invoicing, or serious management fault and may face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and management restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or third-party payments, ignoring sanctions or politically exposed person risks, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, or processing suspicious letters of credit and milestone wires without escalation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory, administrative, and criminal consequences may include substantial fines, transaction restrictions, professional sanctions, asset freezing, and money-laundering imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to EUR 375,000; aggravated forms may carry higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for knowing participation, deliberate blindness, or concealment. Asset confiscation, management prohibition, and judicial travel restrictions may apply; travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file or update the beneficial-owner register, submitting false ownership information, using nominee shareholders to conceal control, or obstructing registry or tax investigations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court orders, fines, registry restrictions, disclosure requirements, and possible criminal penalties for false declarations or concealment. Related tax, money-laundering, and fraud sanctions may apply independently.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may incur personal criminal liability for false or incomplete filings and may face fines, imprisonment where applicable, management bans, and civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book accounts, backdating contracts, fabricating completion certificates, altering invoices, or recording unsupported provisions and receivables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting and tax penalties, rejection of accounts, and criminal sanctions for forgery, use of forged documents, fraudulent accounting, or obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and participating advisers may face personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans, and civil claims by the company, creditors, or tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately deferring revenue, overstating percentage of completion, suppressing variations, capitalizing ordinary costs, or creating unsupported contract-loss provisions to alter taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restatement of taxable income, tax penalties, late-payment interest, audit adjustments across multiple years, and possible fraud or false-accounting prosecution where manipulation is intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for intentional misstatement, breach of management duties, creditor harm, and tax fraud. Professional advisers may also face liability where they knowingly participated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Debt, Thin Capitalization, and Hybrid Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using excessive related-party debt, circular financing, non-commercial guarantees, hybrid instruments, or interest payments designed primarily to erode the French tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Interest deduction limitation, recharacterization of debt as equity or dividend, withholding-tax reassessment, anti-hybrid denial, transfer-pricing adjustment, and penalties for abusive or fraudulent arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability and, where concealment or falsification is proven, criminal tax-fraud or money-laundering liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making payments to sanctioned persons, embargoed jurisdictions, prohibited intermediaries, or undisclosed agents in connection with procurement, construction contracts, or letters of credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment blocking, asset freezing, administrative fines, contract invalidation, procurement exclusion, and criminal sanctions under applicable French, European Union, and international sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, confiscation, and professional or management bans. Ignorance is not a defense where mandatory screening and escalation controls were deliberately avoided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Preserve Tax and Transfer-Pricing Evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lacking intercompany agreements, time records, cost-allocation schedules, engineering deliverables, customs evidence, bank records, or proof supporting related-party services and deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions, adverse inference during audit, transfer-pricing adjustment, documentation penalties, withholding reassessment, and late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for gross negligence or deliberate destruction of records and criminal exposure if evidence was falsified, concealed, or destroyed to obstruct an audit.
